**Status:** Reproduced (simulated Windows on Linux). It also reproduces on the reporter's v9.4.0 and is still present at this checkout (v9.14.0, `@eslint/config-array` 0.18.0).

**Expected:** With cwd `C:\Project`, `F:\foo.js` is treated as outside the base path and ignored, the same way `C:\Other\foo.js` already is.

**Actual:** `F:\foo.js` gets linted. `ESLint#isPathIgnored` returns `false`, `ESLint#lintText` reports `no-undef: 'foo' is not defined.`, and `Linter#verify` returns the same `no-undef` error. As a control, `C:\Other\foo.js` (same drive, outside cwd) is ignored: `File ignored because outside of base path.` from lintText and `No matching configuration found` from Linter.

**Trigger:** A file path on a different drive letter than the base path (cwd).

**Run:** `node repro/cross-drive-ignore.js` (pass an eslint root as the argument to test another version, e.g. `node repro/cross-drive-ignore.js /tmp/e94/node_modules/eslint` after `npm i eslint@9.4.0` there). It exits 1 and prints `BUG REPRODUCED` when the bug is present.

**How the simulation works:** The script loads ESLint with `path` swapped for `path.win32` and `process.cwd()` faked to `C:\Project`. It calls the API directly (Linter, `isPathIgnored`, `lintText`), the same path logic the CLI uses. I didn't run the CLI against a real `F:` drive because this machine is Linux. If you want confirmation on real Windows, I can run it on a Windows machine.

**Likely cause:** `path.win32.relative("C:\\Project", "F:\\foo.js")` returns the absolute `F:\foo.js` instead of a `..`-prefixed path. `@eslint/config-array` decides a file is outside the base path only with `relativeFilePath.startsWith("..")` (in `getConfig`/`isFileIgnored`, `dist/cjs/index.cjs` ~L953, ~L502, ~L1178), so a file on another drive slips through as if it were inside.

**Artifacts:** `repro/cross-drive-ignore.js` is the only change. No production code was changed.
